title: Tenali Raman Tale 122

full_text:
King Krishnadevaraya was troubled by sleepless nights and anxious political worries. He called Tenali Raman to his garden pavilion and asked:
'Tenali, what is the lightest thing in the universe, and what is the heaviest?'

The court scholars answered with textbook physics:
'A swan’s down feather is the lightest, Maharaj! And a boulder of solid iron is the heaviest!'

Tenali Raman shook his head gently:
'No, Maharaj. The scholars measure with brass balances, but life is measured by the soul.
A swan’s down feather is heavy compared to a **Clear Conscience**!
A man who has wronged no soul, spoken no slander, and stolen no copper sleeps upon a bed of stones as lightly as a bird floating upon the morning breeze! No anxiety weighs upon his heart, and his spirit is completely weightless!'

The King sighed, touched by the words: 'And what is the heaviest thing, Tenali?'

Tenali answered with penetrating moral depth:
'The heaviest thing in the universe, Maharaj, is **Guilt**!
A man who has taken an unlawful bribe, betrayed a faithful friend, or oppressed a poor subject may sleep upon cushions of velvet stuffed with swan feathers, yet his heart feels as though a mountain of molten lead were resting upon his chest!
Every creak of the floor terrifies him; every whisper sounds like an accusation; and no wealth on earth can lift the crushing weight of a guilty soul!'

King Krishnadevaraya sat in silence for a long time, absorbing the profound wisdom of Tenali’s counsel.
The Emperor stood up, took Tenali’s hand, and said:
'Tenali, thou hast diagnosed the true ailment of kings.
We worry about defending fortresses, yet the only fortress that truly preserves peace is an unblemished conscience.'

The King reviewed all pending prison petitions that afternoon, pardoned those unjustly detained, lowered taxes on struggling weavers, and that night, the Emperor slept with the peaceful lightness of a clear conscience.
moral: A clear conscience rests lighter than a feather; ill-gotten wealth weighs heavier than lead upon the soul.
